# The Consumer Stocks To Own & Avoid with Evercore's Top Analysts | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 65

First listed: 2026-06-22 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The Consumer Stocks To Own & Avoid with Evercore's Top Analysts | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 65](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yDoSu0BCSiU) - 2026-06-22
- [Substack: The Real State of the American Consumer w/ Three Evercore Analysts | The Real Eisman Playbook](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-real-state-of-the-american-consumer) - 2026-06-22

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Three Evercore analysts separate consumer income pressures from company strategy. They favor value retail, selected restaurant recoveries and Ralph Lauren, while warning about Nike, Lululemon and legacy packaged foods. Eisman adopts the cautious food view and highlights Walmart. Subsequent results support operating dispersion, Walmart membership growth and packaged-food stress, but many causal explanations, valuations and longer-horizon recoveries remain unresolved.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 001. Lower-income consumers have cut restaurant visits after cumulative fast-food price increases outpaced wage growth; casual dining has held up better because its relative pricing is less stretched.

**Unresolved** | David Palmer | explanation | major

[Source at 2:08-6:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yDoSu0BCSiU&t=128s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Income-cohort traffic, cumulative menu pricing and wage comparisons were not independently reproduced; no inference from aggregate retail earnings alone can verify the whole claim.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

**Mixed** | Michael Binetti | explanation | major

[Source at 6:30-9:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yDoSu0BCSiU&t=390s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Ralph Lauren strength and Lululemon weakness show dispersion, but do not establish the full off-price versus department-store comparison or a purely income-driven cause.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

- [Ralph Lauren Q2 FY27 results](https://corporate.ralphlauren.com/pr_261105_Q2FY27-EarningsResults.html) (2026-11-05): Revenue rose 9%, direct-to-consumer comps 10% and average unit retail 9%. Adjusted gross margin rose 250 basis points to 70.5%, with mix and full-price selling support; adjusted EPS rose 22%. Reported margins additionally benefited from tariff refunds.
- [Lululemon Q2 2026 results](https://corporate.lululemon.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/09-03-2026-210528733) (2026-09-03): Revenue fell 4%, Americas revenue 8% and Americas comparable sales 12%. Operating income fell 13% despite $134.5 million tariff refunds. The operating deterioration is verified; the designer-transition explanation is not independently isolated.

<a id="youtube-yDoSu0BCSiU-c004"></a>
### 004. A slower inflation rate does not reverse the accumulated increase in the consumer price level.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 10:49-11:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yDoSu0BCSiU&t=649s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning: The price level compounds prior increases and continues rising at the new positive rate. Restoring an earlier price level requires sufficiently large negative inflation.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

## Framework and tools

- Separate income-cohort demand from brand-specific execution.
- Distinguish accumulated price levels from current inflation.
- Track transactions, ticket, comparable sales and margin separately.
- A good company or rising sales does not automatically imply an attractive valuation.
- Gradual distribution changes can preserve customer and wholesale relationships.
- Differentiate completed earnings recovery from anticipated operating leverage.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Restaurant traffic by income cohort.
- Cumulative menu price versus wages.
- Apparel same-store sales and off-price comparisons.
- Starbucks and Chipotle price charts and earnings expectations.
- Housing lock-in estimates and pro-market size.
- Ralph Lauren AUR and product mix.
- Walmart membership, delivery and advertising.

## Source cautions

Eisman interviews Michael Binetti on apparel, David Palmer on restaurants and food, and Greg Melich on big-box retail. The closing recap from about 3902 seconds is Eisman.
- All transcript segments including the hour-plus ending were read.
- Company results reported after the conversation are outcome checks, not evidence known to the speakers at recording.
- Sponsorship claims and the separate premium-content advertisement are excluded.
- Several figures are proprietary analyst estimates rather than disclosed company data.
